solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Accept fresh cup of tea

indicators.note: something made fresh is newly made up, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone gratefully takes a newly brewed cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh cup of tea' reads as a hot drink being offered, but 'fresh' only signals a new arrangement of the following eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To face up to a difficulty is to stop resisting and come to terms with it, which is one sense of accepting.

clue.text: Axes I throw back into remains of fire

indicators.note: 'back' turns the lobbing round so the word runs right to left
one piece goes into another, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
to lob is to throw in a high arc
ashes are what is left after burning

explanation.surface: Someone tosses old axes onto the embers of a bonfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like the plural noun for chopping tools, but it is the verb: the definition is what someone does when they axe things.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a scheme or rule is to scrap it entirely, so a person who axes things abolishes them.

clue.text: Measure very heavy metal ring

blocks.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
V is the standard abbreviation for very
iron is a dense, heavy metal

explanation.surface: A jeweller weighs a hefty ring made of dark metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' hints at loud rock music and 'ring' at jewellery, but ring is a verb here. EN is a typesetting unit, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To environ something is to surround or encircle it on all sides, a literary verb for forming a circle round.

clue.text: Old man lover won’t get over friend

indicators.note: refusing to get past something means it is left out, so those letters drop away

blocks.note: one's old man is one's father, pa
the word with its final four letters, spelling 'over', taken away

explanation.surface: An elderly man cannot get past his feelings for a former sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Won't get over' sounds like heartbreak, but it tells you to remove the letters O-V-E-R from 'lover', leaving just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Pal is an informal word for a mate or close companion, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Worried less about soccer training grounds

indicators.note: something worried is fretted at and pulled around, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A coach frets less about football than the fitness drills at the club's practice pitches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a person caring less about football; in fact 'Worried' acts on the three words that follow it and the definition sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: These are military or sporting circuits of hurdles, walls and nets built for physical training, hence grounds used for drilling.

clue.text: Master having overnight cases

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the words before it hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster carrying overnight bags for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overnight cases' reads as luggage, but 'cases' is a verb meaning encloses; the answer sits across the join of 'having' and 'overnight'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to master is to control or rule, which is what governing a country or one's temper means.

clue.text: Sees red cracks on parts of hand

blocks.note: has a crack at it means has a go at it, so cracks are goes or attempts
a bunch of bananas is called a hand, so its parts are the individual fruits

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage over split skin on their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracks' and 'hand' paint chapped skin, but cracks are attempts and a hand is the grocer's term for a bunch of bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for becoming furious: to see red is to lose one's temper, and going bananas is slang for the same.

clue.text: Against hybrid lichee as jam ingredient?

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross-bred mix, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: V, short for versus, means against
taken as written; a lichee is the lychee fruit

explanation.surface: A cook objects to using a cross-bred lychee in jam.
explanation.walkthrough: With fruit in the clue, 'jam' looks like preserves; the question mark warns it is a traffic jam, whose ingredients are cars and lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam is made up of stationary cars and lorries, so any car or lorry is one ingredient of it.

clue.text: Religious scholar gets talk cut short

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to rabbit is British slang for chattering on, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk

explanation.surface: A learned cleric's lecture is curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is everyday British slang for talking at length; remove its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher and scholar of religious law, often leading a congregation.

clue.text: Around Nevada, join rally

indicators.note: one word placed around something wraps itself on both sides of it

blocks.note: to coalesce is to come together into one
NV is the US postal code for Nevada

explanation.surface: People in Nevada join a political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' suggests a crowd gathering, but here it is the verb meaning to recover strength; the state goes in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who rallies is regaining health, which is what convalescing means: recovering gradually after illness.

clue.text: Down-and-out ex-pupil in house

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: HO is an abbreviation for house
an old boy, OB, is a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy, now destitute, lives in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: Old boy is the British term for a school's former pupil, abbreviated in crosswords to two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a homeless wanderer with no money, a noun synonym for a down-and-out person.

clue.text: Story teller in trouble over reading?

indicators.note: turned over, a word is flipped so it runs backwards

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
reading is one of the three Rs, so it gives R

explanation.surface: A narrator gets into difficulties over a book reading.
explanation.walkthrough: A story teller is a fibber, not a novelist. Reading is the one genuine R among the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic).
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is an idiom for telling lies, so a story teller in this sense is someone who fibs.

clue.text: Things that should be worn in style

definitions.text: Things that should be worn in style

blocks.note: surface reading: clothes that ought to be put on
setter's reading: a decorating style in which things look deliberately worn and faded

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn' reads as wearing clothes fashionably; it actually means worn out, the look this interior style prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: This interior design fashion uses distressed, faded furniture and fabrics on purpose, so items must look worn to suit it.

clue.text: Green dye put into blue as ordered

indicators.note: something put into another ends up inside it
ordered means arranged afresh, so these letters are set in a new sequence

blocks.note: a stain is a dye or colouring
taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A painter is told to mix green dye into blue.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'dye' and 'blue' in the clue, 'Green' looks like a colour; it is the environmental sense. STAIN goes inside SU-ABLE, the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the environmental sense describes practices that do not deplete resources, which is what sustainable means.

clue.text: It grows light from the East

blocks.note: first meaning: a garden plant, physalis, with papery orange husks
second meaning: a paper lamp of Chinese origin

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like dawn brightening in the east. In fact one name covers both a plant and a paper lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a plant with lantern-shaped seed cases and to a collapsible paper lamp from China.

clue.text: Caught in no-go area, left by night

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a go is a turn, so no go is no turn
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
A is the standard abbreviation for area
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a forbidden zone escapes under cover of darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No-go area' looks like one fixed phrase but splits: NO-TURN holds C after its first two letters, then A and L follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal describes what happens or is active at night, so it is an adjective equivalent to the phrase by night.

clue.text: Do get an agreement of mutual benefit

blocks.note: a do is a party, also called a social
to contract an illness is to get it

explanation.surface: An instruction to secure a deal that helps both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do get' reads as an emphatic order, but Do is a noun, a party, and get means catch, as with a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: In political philosophy this is the implicit pact by which citizens give up some freedoms in exchange for protection, benefiting all.

clue.text: See fit to follow

blocks.note: to con is to study or look over carefully
being on form means being fit and in good condition

explanation.surface: Someone decides it is appropriate to come along behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See fit' looks like the set phrase for deciding something is proper, but the two words are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with rules or go along with what others do, matching the sense of follow as obey.

clue.text: Religious festival managed to include a cross

indicators.note: to include something is to take it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
taken as written
cross means angry, as does mad

explanation.surface: Organisers of a religious celebration fit a cross into the proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: In a religious setting 'cross' suggests the Christian symbol, but it is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic holy month of daytime fasting, a period of religious observance ending in the Eid celebration.

clue.text: Doing things for an author?

blocks.note: surface reading: running errands on a writer's behalf
setter's reading: grammatical words naming the one who does something, of which 'author' itself is an example

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a literary agent's job. The question mark points to grammar: words for a doer, such as author, writer or baker, form a class.
explanation.definitionFit: These grammatical terms name a person or thing performing an action, so author, the one who writes, belongs to the group.

clue.text: Thick soup paste and black olive starter

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: gum is an adhesive paste
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A menu: thick soup, a paste, and black olives to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a course on the menu, but it picks out the first letter of olive.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumbo is a thick Louisiana stew-like soup, often made with okra, a direct example of a hearty soup.

clue.text: Timid type drops small grimace

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so a letter goes missing

blocks.note: a mouse is a shy, timid person
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A shy person gives a little pained expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small grimace' reads as one phrase, but small is the letter S taken out of MOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A moue is a pouting expression of distaste or disappointment, a kind of grimace made with the lips.

clue.text: Magazine content from magazine about bags

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture and hold it, so the words before it contain the answer
brought about, a sequence turns round and runs backwards

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An article taken from a magazine is all about handbags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' appears twice: first as a gun's cartridge holder in the definition, then as plain letters holding the answer backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's magazine holds cartridges, and ammo is the informal short form of ammunition.

clue.text: Getting on top, on horseback

blocks.note: top and best both mean finest
someone on horseback is riding

explanation.surface: A rider climbing into the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on top' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Getting on', as in mounting a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride a horse is to sit astride it, so getting on, in the sense of mounting, is bestriding.

clue.text: Fabled bird seen in stone, it’s said

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: a rock is a stone

explanation.surface: A legendary bird is depicted carved in stone, according to report.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc is the giant bird of the Arabian Nights, in Sinbad's tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a mythical bird of enormous size from Middle Eastern legend, so fabled is exactly right.

clue.text: Red route from Leeds? Arrive on outskirts

indicators.note: to be on something's outskirts is to lie around its edges, enclosing it

blocks.note: to arrive is to come
the M1 motorway runs between London and Leeds; the digit 1 reads as I

explanation.surface: Directions for a road out of Leeds, ending up in the suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's main north-south motorway from London to Leeds; COME splits around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a long-standing term for a communist, and commie is the informal, often derogatory, equivalent.

clue.text: Dry — just about dead as well

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it

blocks.note: sec is the wine term for dry
just and only both mean merely
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A dry wit remarks that something is nearly dead, too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just about' looks like 'nearly', but it splits: ONLY goes about D.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondly introduces an additional point in an argument, so it works like also or in addition.
